attributes.experience:
At Tweag by Modus Create, we offer a unique combination of deep technical expertise and strategic consulting capabilities, with a long-standing commitment to open-source and decentralized systems. EURL Tweag has been in business for over a decade, having started in 2013, and has built a reputation for engineering excellence across critical infrastructure projects.

Since January 2018, we have been continuously engaged with IOG (Input Output Global) on a variety of initiatives within the Cardano ecosystem, including conducting audits and core protocol development. Since May 2021, we have also provided formal audits for the Cardano ecosystem, helping to ensure the reliability and security of mission-critical code.

Our team has played a leading role in the development of Cardano’s core infrastructure, including leading the consensus and ledger teams, implementing the Ouroboros Genesis protocol, and contributing to the design of Ouroboros Peras. We have been involved in nearly all aspects of the core Cardano node, giving us a comprehensive understanding of the system's architecture, roadmap, and strategic direction.

Beyond Cardano, we bring deep, practical experience with Haskell, Rust, and a wide range of technologies used in polyglot projects, enabling us to engineer scalable, secure, and high-performance systems across domains.

As part of Modus Create, a global digital transformation consulting firm, we are backed by a diverse team of strategists, designers, and technologists who help the world’s leading brands build digital advantage. Modus Create specializes in strategic consulting, full lifecycle product development, platform modernization, and digital operations and is an official partner of top-tier technology providers such as Atlassian, AWS, and GitHub. This global reach and cross-disciplinary strength provide our clients with unmatched capabilities throughout the full product development lifecycle.

This proposal reflects our ongoing commitment to advancing Cardano’s mission through rigorous engineering, strategic alignment, and high-impact delivery.
attributes.proposal_name: TWEAG’s  Proposals for multiple core budget projects for Cardano  2025
attributes.resourcing_duration_estimates: Estimates and project costs are noted in the attached document. The total proposal cost is: USD 7,307,520

attributes.problem_statement:
This document outlines Tweag by Modus Create’s proposals for a suite of core infrastructure projects aimed at advancing the technical foundations of the Cardano blockchain. These initiatives focus on novel, high-impact developments across key areas of the Cardano stack. In the months ahead, Tweag intends to collaborate closely with qualified suppliers, DReps, and Intersect to further shape the structure and scope of these engagements.

The proposals presented here represent Tweag’s intended contribution to Cardano’s continued evolution. We invite other ecosystem participants to submit complementary or competitive proposals, and we are open to exploring collaborative partnerships where aligned.

We have consolidated these projects into a single proposal to provide a cohesive view of our core roadmap delivery. We plan to actively seek community input to evaluate whether any of the initiatives should be pursued independently and will adapt our structure accordingly based on that feedback.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
Proposal Benefit
If implemented, this proposal will deliver transformative technical value to the Cardano ecosystem, accelerating development across critical areas of the network stack. The proposed initiatives—ranging from ledger conformance testing and Plutus re-execution tooling, to Genesis synchronization optimization, history expiry, and the development of a Cardano node emulator—are strategically aligned with Cardano’s long-term goals of scalability, performance, and verifiability.

Each project targets a specific technical challenge within the core infrastructure:

Peras, Canonical Ledger State, and Canonical Block and Transaction Diffusion Codecs improve interoperability, clarity, and consistency across the ecosystem.

Conformance Testing for Ledger and Consensus, alongside Black Box Ledger Testing, ensures protocol correctness and future-proofing through robust validation frameworks.

Plutus Script Re-Executor and Block Cost Investigation provide practical tools for performance benchmarking and Plutus optimization, directly benefiting DApp developers and toolmakers.

The Genesis Sync Accelerator and Hoarding Node address network-level performance bottlenecks, improving bootstrap times and reliability.

The Cardano-node-emulator and History Expiry initiative contribute to better testing, debugging, and long-term node sustainability.

Collectively, these projects support developers, researchers, node operators, DReps, and governance actors by reinforcing the reliability, performance, and maintainability of Cardano’s core systems.

The return on investment to the Cardano community is clear:

Faster network upgrades

Reduced onboarding friction

Improved protocol transparency

Better tooling for smart contract teams

More resilient and testable infrastructure

Backed by Tweag by Modus Create and a consortium of trusted ecosystem contributors, this proposal combines deep technical experience with proven delivery capability. It not only addresses current pain points but lays the groundwork for Cardano’s continued success as a scalable, decentralized, and open blockchain platform.

attributes.comment_text: Thank you I will wait for TSC's review before voting.
Are there any Cardano Budget proposals whose scope may currently overlap with this proposal (especially TSC)?
I'm not sure why subcontractors from IOG are proposing their own budgets? I would assume those things would be covered by the IOG budget?

Cardano's technological development is evolving from a centralized model to a more decentralized one where multiple specialized organizations coordinate while making their own unique proposals and contributions. This represents an important step in applying the fundamental blockchain principle of "decentralization" to project management itself.
TWEAG's proposal serves as a significant example within this new model, with great potential to contribute substantially to Cardano's future technological development. Simultaneously, as community governance matures, the collaborative relationships between IOG, TWEAG, and other technical contributors are expected to evolve further.
While all the proposed technical elements are important, this proposal represents a new stage in the relationship between IOG and TWEAG, coming from separate positions. Could you elaborate on how IOG and TWEAG will collaborate to evolve and expand Cardano's critical core technology? I'm also concerned about potential development overlaps.

It seems to me that this proposal has some similarities to items already included in the IOG's “2025 Core Engineering Proposal” and TSC's “Cardano Maintenance and Roadmap Delivery Proposal” as well. Could you please explain how you envision coordinating and assigning roles for these items so that there is no overlap or conflict with the IOG and TSC proposals?

Also, if the TSC proposal were to be approved, it is assumed that the relevant areas would proceed under open bidding and centralized management, and we would like to ask about the background and reasons why Tweag is making these proposals independently.

Please let us know if these proposals are submitted on the assumption that they may be adopted in parallel with other proposals, and if there is any consistency and coordination system in place.

TWEAG's proposal aligns with the objectives of Cardano's 2025 budget, offering particular value through strengthening technical foundations, promoting decentralization, and providing clearly defined deliverables. However, the role division with IOG and potential overlaps with other proposals should be resolved through TSC review and proposal coordination workshops. With proper oversight and accountability mechanisms in place, this proposal appears to hold a justified position within the budget.

While we acknowledge that TWEAK has demonstrated the capability in the past to execute this proposal, and that the proposal aligns with Cardano's roadmap and, according to our experts, is technically feasible, we note a significant degree of overlap with initiatives led by IOG and the Technical Steering Committee (TSC).

Our recommendation is therefore contingent upon TWEAK's participation in a reconciliation workshop to address these overlaps. Cardano's treasury—and its delegated representatives (dReps)—should not be expected to fund substantially similar proposals multiple times.

In conclusion, recognizing the past vendor relationship between IOG and TWEAK, we believe there is potential for a point of alignment and collaboration.

Thank you for your thoughtful feedback. We would like to emphasize that our proposal is aligned with the Cardano roadmap and does not conflict with any of the ongoing IOE-led initiatives. While we recognize there is some overlap with the Technical Steering Committee's (TSC) proposal, we view this as an opportunity for constructive collaboration rather than duplication.

We welcome the suggestion of a reconciliation workshop and are fully committed to participating. Our aim is to ensure complementarity, not redundancy, and to make the best use of Cardano’s treasury by working transparently with all stakeholders involved.

From a workshop, the North American Community Hub summarized feedback on TWEAG’s proposal. 

The group did not reach a clear consensus on approving or rejecting Proposal 205 for Core budget funding. 

Participants were divided, with some supporting TWEAG’s strong reputation, thorough documentation, and alignment with Core needs, while others raised concerns about the steep cost, excessive scope, unclear distinction between core and value-add components, and questions about past IOG funding. 

The lack of transparency on previous contracts and the high price tag ($27,000/month per FTE) fueled reluctance, with some questioning whether the proposal duplicates existing work. 

While there’s cautious support due to TWEAG’s expertise, the group remains unsure, recommending further clarification on scope, costs, and funding history before a Core budget commitment.

Conditionally YES 

The contents of the proposal should be rationally broken down, DRep should vote on each item, and the results should be reflected in the proposal. Please have the TSC review and make any overlap adjustments. In order to keep the total expenditure for 2025 within 200M, please separate items that can be spent in 2026 into items that can be spent without any problems and items that should be spent by December 2025.

Technical Steering Committee Review:

The TSC provides the following advice as a brief summary to aid the DReps and community in forming a budget proposal. A proper evaluation would take significantly longer than the time available: the TSC anticipates that such a review will be necessary prior to agreeing any contracts. This may, for example, involve determining milestones and timelines, where these are necessary or otherwise revising the original proposal.

Overview:

This represents a compendium of 11 projects by one provider. Two projects align with clear needs. Others fill apparently sensible niches, but these need community or technical validation before serious work is commenced. Overall value for money depends on how successful each project is, and on how useful the work is.

Recommendation:

Break the proposal into individual sub-projects, which can be considered independently. Evaluate the need/demand for each sub-project. Determine all dependencies where these are unclear. Clearly identify efforts by sub-contractors, where these are needed, and confirm that necessary effort is available. Confirm the demand for work with Technical Working Groups or other users as appropriate. Clearly identify start and end SRLs for each project.

Detailed Comments:

The Tweag proposal covers $7.3M of spend at a rate of $332,160 per developer year (FTE), for a total of approximately 22 developer years of effort over an unspecified period (at least 10 months). The proposal covers part of one core roadmap item (Ouroboros Peras), one core maintenance item (Cardano node emulator), plus 9 additional sub-projects. Each of these projects is standalone and can be considered independently. The proposal uses a fixed price per milestone approach. Some gating is possible. SRLs are not clearly identified, but information is generally provided that allows goals to be judged.

Peras. The Peras sub-project covers part of the work that is needed to develop Peras, at about SRL 5-6 (initial implementation). Further work is needed to complete and deploy the solution. The proposal identifies three milestones, but doesn’t give timelines for completion. There is an unstated dependency on the Cardano network team. The work considers only “pre-alpha” Peras rather than “alpha” Peras, which is less susceptible to cooldowns, but which is still in a research stage.

Technical Steering Committee Review (Part 2):

Cardano node emulator maintenance. The Cardano node emulator tool forms part of the Intersect repositories. It is used by various DApp developers to validate and test Plutus scripts. The project proposes to use two named maintainers, both of whom possess relevant developer skills. Various improvements will be made, but the tool will not be further developed. Confirmation of value should be obtained from stakeholders.

Canonical ledger state. This is a sensible project proposal that would directly support alternative node implementations and tooling such as DB-Sync. Potential users should be involved in this work.

Black box ledger conformance testing and conformance testing of consensus. These are two similar projects for different parts of the Cardano node. They depend on active members of the ledger and consensus developer teams to integrate and respond to the tests. Confirmation of the value of each approach should be sought from each of those teams.

Plutus script re-executor. This project aims to improve user experience for DApp developers by providing off-chain script execution capabilities. The value of such an approach needs to be determined with DApp developers.

Genesis Sync Accelerator. This project aims to improve user experience by reducing the load on stake pool relays while syncing using Ouroboros Genesis. It is unclear whether this will be beneficial in practice, however: major load will only occur when syncing a full node from the Genesis block.

Canonical Block and Transaction Diffusion Codecs. This project will deal with technical debt by removing unnecessary EBBs (these were required in the Byron era) and ledger era tags. This is a useful improvement that would simplify the codebase, and that has previously been proposed by the consensus team.

Hoarding node. The hoarding node collates blocks from across the Cardano network to allow information to be inspected in the event of bugs, undesirable transactions etc. This is a potentially useful service that could reduce the cost of finding fixes. There is an ongoing cost to maintain the node and to operate the service. The value should be confirmed with the relevant Technical Working Groups.

Technical Steering Committee Review (Part 3)

Block cost investigation. This project would investigate worst case block construction costs, helping to inform future implementation and parameter decisions. This work would need to interface with Intersect’s parameter committee, which makes recommendations on parameter settings.

History Expiry. This project would truncate historical chain data, relying on some future version of eg Mithril to securely supply snapshot data. This would have benefits in terms of storage requirements of old chain data, but relies on secure snapshots being available. Sufficient history would need to be kept to allow disaster recovery and to support all possible transactions. The interaction with the new UTXO-HD storage solution also needs to be investigated.

Tweag is an experienced and well established software development company whose employees have been working on Cardano for over 7 years. They provide highly skilled software developers, including ones with significant Haskell expertise. The proposal involves a team of over 20 developers.

The link to the proposed collaborators needs to be clarified. Are they necessary to carry out the work? Have they confirmed their willingness to work on the proposed projects? How much effort is expected from each partner? Will costs be passed through directly, or will Tweag take a profit from any difference in pricing.

Security audits need to be clarified. When are they required? How will their quality be assured?

No risk assessment is done for any of the projects.

Milestones and timelines need to be confirmed for each of the projects.
